paper_metadata.title: Predictors of Cognitive Impairment After Stroke: A Prospective Stroke Cohort Study

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides a clear description of the source population, recruitment period, and inclusion/exclusion criteria. However, there is a significant selection bias noted by the authors: the analyzed sample had lower NIHSS scores (minor strokes) compared to those excluded, which limits the representativeness of the stroke population.

items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: This was a prospective and consecutive study conducted in the Neurology Department of Huashan Hospital affiliated with Fudan University, which is an advanced stroke center in Shanghai, China.
items.reasoning: The setting and nature of the population (acute ischemic stroke patients at a tertiary center) are clearly defined.

items.evidence_snippet: From June 2017 to May 2018, there were 247 subjects diagnosed with acute stroke onset within one week of screening, and 179 patients who met the inclusion criteria were included in our cohort
items.reasoning: The study uses a consecutive recruitment strategy from a defined screening pool.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: The inclusion criteria were as follows: 1) diagnosis made according to the 2013 American Heart Association (AHA)/American Stroke Association (ASA) stroke definition, 2) stroke onset within the last 7 days...
items.reasoning: Detailed criteria including diagnostic standards and time-from-onset are provided.

items.label: Adequate study participation
items.prompt: There is adequate participation in the study by eligible individuals
items.evidence_snippet: 68 patients were excluded from the cohort for the following reasons: aphasia (n = 27), conscious disturbance (n = 12)...
items.reasoning: While recruitment was consecutive, a large number of eligible patients were excluded due to stroke severity (aphasia, consciousness), which the authors admit creates a bias toward minor strokes.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The attrition rate was approximately 19% (34/179). The authors performed a robust comparison between completers and non-completers, finding no significant differences in key baseline characteristics, which suggests the loss to follow-up was likely not informative.

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis
items.prompt: Response rate (i.e., proportion of study sample completing the study and providing outcome data) is adequate.
items.evidence_snippet: One hundred forty-five subjects completed a 6–12-month follow-up visit
items.reasoning: 145/179 (81%) is generally considered an acceptable follow-up rate in prognosis studies.

items.label: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out

items.evidence_snippet: The remaining 34 subjects did not participate in the follow-up visit for the following reasons: 1) rehabilitation in admission (13 subjects), 2) not in Shanghai (13 subjects), or 3) refusal (8 subjects).
items.reasoning: The study tracked and reported the reasons for dropout.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The statistical methods are generally sound, including collinearity checks and AUROC analysis. However, the sample size (n=145) is relatively small for a model with 5 predictors (violating the '10 events per variable' rule given 77 PSCI cases, though borderline), and there is no external validation, which the authors acknowledge.

items.label: Presentation of analytical strategy

items.evidence_snippet: Variables showing significant differences (p < 0.05) between groups were identified as confounding factors in subsequent binomial logistic regression analysis.
items.reasoning: The study used a standard (though univariate-led) approach to variable selection and checked for collinearity.

items.prompt: The selected statistical model is adequate for the design of the study.

items.reasoning: Logistic regression is appropriate for the binary outcome (PSCI vs. PSNCI).
